The KB-era index.html that used to sit in this directory was DELETED 2026-08-27: it was retired as a visual target on 2026-08-26 and kept only because ci:mockup-coverage required a parity.json beside any index.html, which is a gate keeping a dead file alive. The target is the patterns in PUBLIC_UI.md, built from components/site/v3. THIS FILE STILL BINDS: requiredComponents is what stops a page silently losing a section, and ci:mockup-parity reads it with or without a mockup.
competitiveTarget: Utility comparison page: side-by-side property table. noindex — not an SEO surface. The landing state is the competitive surface: Redfin and Zillow open their compare screens on the visitor's own saved thumbnails, and this page has no saved-homes rail to open on. It wins instead by showing the finished object to a visitor who arrives with nothing — four real homes for sale right now, in the real table, labelled as an example, each one a single tap into their own comparison.
note: E-HOMES-SEARCH 2026-08-13. Migrated /compare chrome onto the v3 barrel. Chrome: layout mounts V3Chrome (sticky, in flow). This page does not remount it. V3Breadcrumb belowNav=false. V3Footer outside <main>. Page contract carried unchanged: robots noindex,follow, revalidate 60, canonical /compare, DAL fetch (getListingTiles by listNumbers AND listingKeys, dedup, getListingDetailPhotos), CompareClient props, BreadcrumbList JSON-LD, V3SectionTracker pageType=compare. Shared /compare?ids= links keep resolving. Dual objectives unchanged. Capture does not live on this route. KB-era deletions: SmoothScrollProvider, KbBreadcrumb, KbFooter, kb-root, kb.css, navy header band. AICompare deleted 2026-08-18 (never wired). MetadataBlock and KbSectionTracker stay on non-v3 registers. SITE-50 (2026-09-09): the empty state left V3Quiet for V3Slots, a new barrel pattern. The taste table scored this class 29 with the verdict 'an empty form label, not a product demo'; Quiet has no slot, no table and no figure by contract, so the fix could never be a prop on Quiet. Two more defects were fixed in the same change: the H1 sat in a bare <header> with no measure and no gutter and was clipped at x=0 at both 1440 and 375, and the visually-hidden spans inside the new table escaped their scroll container (no positioned ancestor) and made the document scroll sideways at 375 — html.scrollWidth 602 against a 375 viewport.

tasteReview.beats: Redfin's and Zillow's compare screens open on the visitor's own saved homes with large listing cards and a highlight-differences control. This page wins a live four-home MLS sample and a named Oregon Data Share timestamp on first load. It loses photo scale, a winner or delta reading, and any 375 layout that can actually hold four homes.

defects.finding: The houses are the subject and they render as 64px stamps; an editorial compare would make the four exteriors the spectacle, not table chrome. replaceWith: V3Carousel of the four street views as the opening object, or column heads at photo-card scale.

At 375 the second column is sliced through 40 McKinley, Add thi, and $529,99, so four homes cannot be compared in one view. replaceWith: V3Segmented (two homes at a time) or V3Sheet compare, not a cropped spreadsheet scroller.
Four identical outline Add this home buttons turn the comparison into a repeated form kit instead of a reading of which house to keep.
The lengths under Price, Price / sq ft, Sq ft and Lot are hairline underlines, not a glanceable comparison; they do not survive a still as data.
Year built prints as 2,005, 2,006, 2,021 and 2,003; years do not take thousands separators.
40 McKinley Avenue opens on a kitchen while the other three columns open on street exteriors, so the four homes do not read as the same kind of object.

Nothing names a winner or a spread; $849,000 sits next to $529,999 with no sentence that one is $319,001 more, so the job of compare is left to the reader's arithmetic. replaceWith: V3Sheet compare with a per-row mark, or a claim that states the spread.
The fold spends itself on muted explanation (claim plus SAMPLE caption) before any house is large enough to look at; the page still opens as eyebrow, display heading, paragraph, then a ledger.
Addresses wrap to uneven depths (Porcupine Drive on three lines at 375, others cropped mid-word), so the column heads do not share one rhythm.

No hover, tap, scrub or toggle in the still rewards more data; Add this home leaves the sample instead of revealing a difference, a sort, or a two-up. replaceWith: beUI tabs / V3Segmented to pick which pair, plus a row hover that states the delta.

tasteReview.rebaselineReason: evaluatorModel and shotsHash differ: SITE-50's 53 was claude-sonnet-5 on shots that still led with four dashed empty slots (shotsHash sha256:f541dd6d); this mark is grok-4.6 on new first-viewport shots after SITE-65 made the live sample the opening. Same rubricVersion v1-2026-09-08. Mechanical accept holds: four listing photographs and prices in the 1440 fold, no dashed empty Add-a-home tray.
tasteReview.verdict: Better than a 53: the dashed empty tray is gone and the first screen is the comparison itself, which is the job. It is still a spreadsheet under a display heading — stamp photos, hairline bars you have to hunt, a 375 crop that hides two of the four homes, and four identical outline buttons, so it is not yet a page anyone would screenshot.
